acceptance.given: The six-case Matrix Case execution matrix is run and emits a per-case execution record.

oracle.expected: All six records identify fixture and state identities, and every identity is distinct from the corresponding identities of the other five cases.
forbidden: Cases sharing fixtures or state contrary to the distinctness requirement
oracle.observable: The six-case execution record contains six attributable fixture/state identity pairs with no duplicates.

acceptance.then: All six Matrix Cases have executed with distinct fixtures and state.
acceptance.when: When the Matrix Case execution matrix runs.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the matrix with a duplicated fixture or state identity; the structural distinctness check must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Emit and validate explicit fixture and state identities for each of six Matrix Cases, rejecting duplicates or ambiguity.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve matrix schema and existing case fields; add explicit identity validation without mutating historical records.

slice_hint.state_transition: matrix cases lack proven distinct fixture/state identities -> six attributable, pairwise-distinct identity pairs
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Matrix evaluation terminates as pass only when six records exist and fixture and state identities are pairwise distinct; otherwise fail.

acceptance.given: Frozen obligations provide independent oracles, assertions, behavior RED distinctions, and non-runtime failure-family distinctions for compilation.

oracle.expected: The compiled coverage retains every independent oracle and assertion, preserves behavior RED distinctions, and preserves each non-runtime failure family as a separate executable or structural check.
oracle.observable: Compiled obligation contracts can be enumerated one-to-one with the frozen oracle/assertion and failure-distinction records.

acceptance.when: When compiling or repairing bound obligations.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Compile coverage after removing or merging one oracle, assertion, RED distinction, or non-runtime failure family; the preservation audit must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Compile and audit independent verification contracts without merging their assertions or failure distinctions, while retaining runtime RED semantics.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing gate and replay schemas; no historical evidence rewrite and no weakening of failure-family semantics.

slice_hint.state_transition: independent verification distinctions declared but not audited -> every oracle/assertion and distinction retained and checked
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Compilation passes only when a preservation audit proves one-to-one retention of all frozen oracle, assertion, RED, and non-runtime failure distinctions.

acceptance.given: The retained S41 skill-replay-contract fixture is evaluated through the declared S41 test-author selector.

oracle.expected: The evaluation identifies the fixture's declared role and requires a distinct real assertion as behavior proof; the fixture's existence alone contributes no behavior proof.
forbidden: The fixture's existence is treated as proof of behavior.
The fixture is assigned a role beyond its declaration.
oracle.observable: The S41 selector produces separate fixture-role and behavior-proof assertion results.

acceptance.then: The retained S41 fixture remains role-limited and non-probative by existence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Fail the S41 selector when the fixture is used beyond its declared role or when fixture presence is accepted as behavior evidence.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add an S41 fixture-role boundary assertion that requires behavior proof to be supplied by a separate real assertion.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only the S41 role-boundary evaluation; retain the fixture and its historical role unchanged.

slice_hint.state_transition: The S41 fixture moves from unqualified retained input to explicitly role-limited, non-probative input.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The S41 selector has separate passing checks for declared-role fidelity and independent behavior proof, and rejects a presence-only proof.

acceptance.given: The retained S7 and S13 fixtures are evaluated with their declared S7 and S13 test-author selectors.

oracle.expected: Each retained S7 and S13 fixture is validated only for its declared role, and the selectors require independent real assertions to establish behavior.
forbidden: Treating the existence of a retained fixture as proof of behavior.
Using retained fixtures outside their actual declared roles.
oracle.observable: The S7 and S13 selectors each report fixture-role boundary results separately from behavior-proof results.

acceptance.then: The retained S7 and S13 fixtures remain role-limited and cannot establish behavior merely by existing.
acceptance.when: When using or evaluating retained S7 and S13 fixtures.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Fail the applicable S7 or S13 selector if a retained fixture is repurposed or fixture existence is accepted as behavior proof.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add S7 and S13 fixture-role boundary assertions that reject presence-only behavior evidence and require independent real assertions.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only the S7/S13 role-boundary checks; preserve retained fixtures and their declared roles.

slice_hint.state_transition: S7 and S13 fixture use becomes explicitly role-specific, with presence-only proof rejected.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Both selectors demonstrate declared-role-only fixture use and obtain behavior proof from separate real assertions.
